_note: Typical, balanced wording for common clauses in Indian rental and employment agreements. Written by the LexLocal team as a reference point for 'unusual wording' detection only. These are not model clauses and not legal advice.
rent: The Tenant shall pay a monthly rent of Rs. 20,000 on or before the 5th day of every month.
The monthly rent shall be paid in advance by bank transfer to the account of the Landlord.
The rent shall be increased by 5% on renewal of this agreement.
security deposit: The Tenant has paid an interest-free refundable security deposit equal to two months' rent.
The security deposit shall be refunded without interest at the time of vacating the premises, after deducting any unpaid rent or charges.
The Landlord shall refund the deposit within 30 days of the Tenant handing over vacant possession, less reasonable deductions for damage beyond normal wear and tear.
term: This agreement shall be for a period of 11 months commencing from the start date.
The agreement may be renewed for a further period on mutually agreed terms.
The Licensor grants the Licensee a leave and license to occupy the flat for a period of 11 months from the start date.
lock-in period: Both parties agree to a lock-in period of 3 months during which neither party may terminate this agreement except for breach.
notice period: Either party may terminate this agreement by giving one month's written notice to the other party.
After the lock-in period, either party may end this agreement by giving thirty days' prior written notice.
termination for breach: The Landlord may terminate this agreement if the Tenant fails to pay rent for two consecutive months after giving 15 days' written notice to cure the default.
maintenance and repairs: Minor day-to-day repairs shall be carried out by the Tenant, and major or structural repairs shall be the responsibility of the Landlord.
The Tenant shall keep the premises in good condition, subject to normal wear and tear.
inspection and entry: The Landlord may inspect the premises at a reasonable time after giving at least 24 hours' notice to the Tenant.
use of premises: The Tenant shall use the premises for residential purposes only.
The Tenant shall not sublet or part with possession of the premises without the prior written consent of the Landlord.
utilities: Electricity and water charges as per actual meter readings shall be paid by the Tenant.
late payment: If rent is not paid within 10 days of the due date, the Tenant shall pay a late fee of Rs. 500.
dispute resolution: Any dispute arising out of this agreement shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the courts where the premises are located.
Any dispute shall be referred to a sole arbitrator appointed by mutual consent of both parties.
liability and indemnity: Each party shall be responsible for loss or damage caused by its own negligence.
salary: The Employee shall be paid an annual cost to company as set out in the annexure, payable monthly.
Salary shall be paid on or before the last working day of each month.
probation: The Employee shall be on probation for a period of six months, which may be extended by up to three months with written reasons.
employment notice: After confirmation, either party may terminate employment by giving 30 days' written notice or salary in lieu of notice.
During probation, either party may terminate employment by giving 15 days' written notice.
leave: The Employee is entitled to paid leave each calendar year as per the Company's leave policy, in addition to public holidays.
confidentiality: The Employee shall keep confidential all non-public information of the Company during and after employment.
post-employment restrictions: For a period of 6 months after leaving, the Employee shall not solicit clients of the Company with whom the Employee worked.
intellectual property: Work product created by the Employee in the course of employment shall belong to the Company.
working hours: Normal working hours are 9 hours per day, five days a week, with reasonable flexibility.
governing law: This agreement shall be governed by the laws of India and the courts at the city where it is signed shall have jurisdiction.
bonus: The Employee may be eligible for an annual performance bonus as per the Company's bonus policy.
appointment: The Company appoints the Employee to the position of Software Engineer with effect from the joining date, reporting to the team manager.
stamp duty: The stamp duty and registration charges for this agreement shall be shared equally by both parties.
general compliance: The Tenant shall comply with the bye-laws of the housing society as applicable to all residents.
